subject: Finova — Decision Criteria Clarification & Stakeholder Mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Leung <sara.leung@finova.com>, Tom Hsu <thsu@finova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Finova discovery recap — decision criteria & next steps

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — really helpful to hear more about the Finova use case and the buying process. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can put together a concise package for procurement/legal and the economic buyer.

Quick recap of what I took away:
- Primary workload: document-to-text search and on-demand chat for internal ops (customer support + underwriting).
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity with VPC peering (need data isolation and predictable throughput).
- Decision criteria called out on the call:
  - Latency: p95 under ~200ms for short-form chat flows (1–2 turns), p95 < 400ms for longer sessions;
  - Cost target: unit economics that keep per-conversation cost comparable to current hosted baseline (you mentioned wanting a ~30% reduction vs current provider for core workloads);
  - SLA: target 99.9% availability and incident response playbook + on-call contact for production incidents.
- Security/compliance: SOC 2 + DPA required; security questionnaire in procurement.
- Economic buyer / procurement: Tom is the VP/owner; procurement timeline targeting decision by end of Q2.

Clarifying asks so we can tailor the procurement package:
1) Can you confirm the economic buyer who will sign (Tom?) and whether procurement requires a PO or signature-based SOW?
2) For latency targets, are the numbers above (p95 <200ms short flows) measured end-to-end from app to model response, or do you prefer we provide both model-only inference p95 and end-to-end guidance?
3) For cost, any guardrails you can share on monthly token volume so we can model committed vs on-demand pricing? (ballpark is fine)

Next steps I propose:
- I’ll send a one-page decision criteria summary and a stakeholder map for you to confirm (attaching v1) — will include pricing/SLAs options for Dedicated vs Private.
- Rafael (cc’d) will follow up with a short tech note on latency measurement methodology and typical p95 numbers on our Dedicated offering.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min call next week with Tom to walk procurement checklist and timeline.

Attaching: finova-stakeholder-map-v1.xlsx and a short decision-criteria PDF that summarizes options.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Sara Leung <sara.leung@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <thsu@finova.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova discovery recap — decision criteria & next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the thorough recap and for pulling the attachments together. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Confirming economic buyer is Tom Hsu (VP Engineering); he’ll own the procurement signature but legal will need to sign the DPA.
- Procurement prefers signature-based SOW + PO for platform purchases; they will need an initial quote and an estimate of committed capacity to produce a PO.
- Latency: the numbers you captured are in line with our expectations. We measure p95 end-to-end (client->model->client). It would be helpful if you can provide both model-only inference p95 and end-to-end guidance so we can instrument accordingly.
- Cost/volume: rough monthly volume today for these flows is ~250M tokens/month (prompt+response). We’re planning for 2x growth in 12 months. Pricing sensitivity: ideally total inference spend under $12k/month initially for the pilot, with predictable step-up as we scale.
- Security: SOC 2 Type II, DPA, and an initial security questionnaire (I’ll attach our standard security spreadsheet after this thread). Legal will want to see data residency and key management options.
- Timeline: procurement + legal expectation is 6–8 weeks once we have a quote and security artifacts. Tom and I are aiming for contractual lock by the end of Q2.

I’ve attached an edited stakeholder map (finova-stakeholder-map-v1.xlsx) with who will be involved on our side — please confirm your internal stakeholders and resource owners.

Sara
Head of Risk Ops | Finova
sara.leung@finova.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Sara Leung <sara.leung@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Tom Hsu <thsu@finova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-23T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Finova discovery recap — decision criteria & next steps

Thanks Sara — helpful context. A couple notes from the infra/tech side on how we’ll present latency and SLA options:

- We will provide two latency numbers in the packet: model-only inference p95 (measured in our Dedicated runtime, from request reach of the model-serving container to response) and end-to-end guidance (estimated network + app overhead). For Dedicated in region-us-west, model-only p95 for typical chat flows (short prompts, 1–2 turns) is usually ~80–140ms depending on sequence length and batching.
- For SLA, we can offer a 99.9% availability SLO for Dedicated with an incident response SLA (on-call pager + 2-hour initial response for Sev1). We’ll include an operational runbook and on-call contact in the package.
- Regarding cost modeling: with your ~250M tokens/month baseline, we’ll prepare two scenarios — committed Dedicated discount (monthly commit) and an on-demand model with autoscale — to show unit economics and expected monthly spend.

I’ll draft the technical appendix for the procurement packet and share later today.

—Rafael
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rafael_mendes@redwood.com

Marissa / Team —

Appreciate the recap. Two quick asks from my side before we move to procurement:
1) Can you send a one-page summary showing (a) the Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs we discussed, (b) expected p95 numbers for each, and (c) a pricing estimate given our ~250M tokens/month baseline?
2) Please include the DPA + SOC 2 evidence (or link to SOC 2 report) so my legal team can start the review in parallel.

If you can get those materials over in the next 4 business days we’ll have enough to open the procurement request and target PO issuance within 6–8 weeks.
